A Therapist’s take :: As a mental health professional, journaling is something I often suggest to people for a myriad of reasons and benefits. I always make sure to remind them that there is no wrong or right way to journal. Personally I have only done poetic journaling and stream of consciousness journaling. I have typically saved my more profound reflecting and processing for my own therapy sessions. However, after just one week with Reflection: AI journal & coach, I can see this becoming a regular practice for me (which I’m sure my therapist would agree is a great habit to pick up). I can also see it being a go-to recommendation that I make when someone is struggling with journaling. Not only is it helpful with cultivating insight, it can also be quite fun to use the AI features that make one “go deeper” or provide  “coaching” and “summaries”. Lastly, as a therapist that believes mental health services should be accessible to all, I make it a point to offer a sliding scale. Reflection: AI journal & coach aligns with this value I dearly hold and offers a “scholarship” for the premium version of the app. With this scholarship, the app allows people to sign up for a year of the premium version on a sliding scale based on what they can afford. Thus making its premium version widely accessible. What’s additionally wonderful is that if you’re just starting out and building a new habit, you don’t even need to sign up for premium; the standard version of the app is free to use! I hope you’ll enjoy this tool as much as I have! Happy journaling!

This usually prompts me to leave more comprehensive details on my experiences, which are essential for more effective personal reflections.

Furthermore, after having typed down your reflection for a certain day, a monthly review will be made available to you after, well, a month. This allows you to have a greater view of what had happened in the past, and how you may have changed your attitude or tune about your past experience. In short: it is a FANTASTIC reflection application.

Experienced, procrastinating, struggling, and novice journalers alike  will find safe harbors and stout winds herein.
